viewer_structure.include_mechanism: `include!("examples/NN_name.rs")` at crate root, main.rs:170-7902 (135 lines), interleaved in no order (29 is followed by 103..126, then 30..36, then 104..108, then 37..51). Fragments are not modules: every fn/struct/const lands in the bin crate root namespace.
viewer_structure.dispatch_mechanism: No registry, no trait objects. Six parallel match statements keyed on `enum Scene`, plus a string match for panel titles and a second match for pane bodies: (1) build_scene_model main.rs:3566-3731, (2) solver_kind main.rs:2645-2704 (default `_ => Xpbd`), (3) physics_audit main.rs:2770-3413, (4) label main.rs:2056-2211, (5) description main.rs:2214-2635, (6) scene-pane title main.rs:5608-5714, and (7) the pane-body match main.rs:5724-5957 (125 Scene arms). Scene::ALL (main.rs:1898-2053) is a third hand-maintained list of all 151 variants, used only for the dropdown.
viewer_structure.execution_loop_summary: Startup: `Sim::build_scene(Scene::Pile)` (main.rs:385) -> build_scene_model -> finalize: Engine::new_gpu().expect(...) at main.rs:3803, adapter_label from engine.adapter_info() (3807-3810), `device`/`queue` cloned (3811-3812), then unconditional `upload_to_device` of model, state_a, state_b, control, contacts (3814-3827), then build_solver(engine, model, scene.solver_kind()) at 3830 and four scene-specific `matches!(scene, ...)` retunes (3835-3885). Per frame the Update chain is: pre-step controllers -> step_simulation -> sync_transforms/sync_cloth_mesh (main.rs:406-419). step_simulation (4494-4793) first early-returns for ~110 of the 151 scenes via seven consecutive `if sim.scene == ...` / `matches!` blocks (4520-4670) — each host-driven scene runs its own update_* system instead. Otherwise, for SUBSTEPS_PER_FRAME=10 substeps of FIXED_DT=1/600 s: pipeline.collide(model, state_a, contacts) then contacts.upload_to_device(), an XPBD-only host->device upload of body_q/body_qd (4704-4707, gated by `matches!(solver, SolverBackend::Xpbd(_))`), solver.step(...) into state_b, `std::mem::swap(state_a, state_b)`, then a full body_q/body_qd (and joint_q/joint_qd, particle_q/particle_qd) download_from_device per substep (4714-4740).
viewer_structure.cpu_gpu_boundary: Every scene's model/state/control/contacts buffers are uploaded once in finalize (main.rs:3814-3827) regardless of whether the scene ever steps. Readback happens inside step_simulation's substep loop (main.rs:4714-4740) and the renderer only reads `state_a.body_q.host()` in sync_transforms (4795-4800) and `particle_q.host()` in sync_cloth_mesh. Scene switches reuse the same Engine (`Sim::rebuild` comment main.rs:3906-3910: 'scene switches must not call Engine::new_gpu() again').

connection_health.summary: The three crates are connected by exactly two real edges: molla->all subcrates (mostly one-line re-exports) and molla_viewer->molla. molla-sim is the only subcrate with a clean, widely-consumed contract (6 sibling crates, 23 files in molla-geometry alone) and no outbound dependency beyond core/math/storage. The facade is where the wiring goes wrong: it is a re-export trampoline whose kernels/prelude give 400+ names one flat namespace, and it is exercised in-repo only by the viewer.
broken_or_weak_links: molla's dependency list is 7/15 stale (see unused_cargo_deps) — half the declared edges exist only on paper.

crates/molla/src/kernels/mod.rs:118-120 re-exports ~400 identifiers from molla-kernels in one `pub use`, including a whole embedded tire simulation stack; the facade cannot be consumed without admitting all of it.
molla_viewer never depends on molla-sim, molla-core, molla-solvers or molla-kernels directly, so the facade's shape is never pressure-tested by a second consumer.
No workspace crate other than molla_viewer depends on molla, so there is no in-tree consumer proving the public surface is coherent.
missing_coverage: No reset/pause/step contract per scene: `R` maps to Sim::reset (main.rs:4218) which only restores body_q/body_qd/particle_q from model.initial_* (4031-4091). Only 8 of 135 fragments define their own `fn reset` (109_warpfemconvdiffdg.rs:3486, 112_warpfemstokestransfer.rs, 121_tire_traction.rs, 47_fem_heat.rs, 48_fem_beam.rs, 50_fem_stokes.rs, 96_dgburgersshock.rs, 97_shallowwaterdambreak.rs); the rest expose ad-hoc `user_reset: bool` flags inside their own state structs, so every scene resets differently and most have no reset at all.

PhysicsAuditStatus has no arm for 'host-driven CPU demo that is not physics' — scene_smoke/scene_correctness in crates/molla/tests exercise solver scenes, not viewer scenes, so the audit table is the only per-scene record and nothing checks it against behaviour.
